name: Mercaptan sweetening (Merox)
principle: Merox converts malodorous mercaptans to disulfides (4 RSH + O2 -> 2 RSSR + 2 H2O) over a catalyst in alkaline conditions. For LPG and light naphtha, an extraction variant uses caustic to pull mercaptans out and air regenerates the caustic. For kerosene and jet fuel, a fixed-bed sweetening variant oxidises them in place on catalyst-impregnated charcoal.

process_steps.name: Extraction of mercaptans into caustic (LPG, light naphtha)
Air oxidation of spent caustic to disulfides
Water wash, salt dryer and clay filter

performance.basis: sweetening is usually enough for straight-run kerosene to meet it; the page gives no treated-product mercaptan figure

advantages: Same chemistry across LPG, naphtha and jet
limitations: Does not remove total sulfur, only converts mercaptans
